userStories.title: Thread data, kill switch and runner thread capacity
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the `ChatThread`, `ChatMessage` and `FleetThreadTurn` models, `FleetJob.threadId`, `Runner.threadCapacity` (with admin PATCH), the `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` config flag and the migration with its partial unique index.

**Motivation** — Without this feature there is no record to chat on and no way to bound how many thread sessions a runner hosts.

**Approach** — Config: `IFleetConfig` gains `threadsEnabled: boolean` from `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` (`'true'` = on, anything else or unset = off). `Runner.threadCapacity` is server-only (admin PATCH); the runner never reads it. `RunnerRecord`, `RunnerPatch` (`apps/api/src/fleet/runners/domain/runner.domain.ts`), `RunnerDto`, `UpdateRunnerDto` gain `threadCapacity` (DTO: integer 0..16); `RunnersService.update` and `prisma-runner.repository.ts` carry it. `testFleetConfig` (`apps/api/src/common/test-helpers/fleet-config.ts`) gains `threadsEnabled: false`. `PARTIAL_UNIQUE_INDEXES` in `apps/api/test/helpers/partial-indexes.ts` gains `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "ChatThread_active_repo_feature_key" ON "ChatThread" ("repoId", "feature") WHERE "status" = 'ACTIVE'`, because integration schemas come from `prisma db push`, which cannot create partial indexes; the same statement appears verbatim in the migration (pinned by the partial-indexes unit spec under apps/api/test/unit/fleet). Migration: `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261013090000_chat_threads/migration.sql`. Regenerate `openapi.json` via `bun run api:export-spec` for `RunnerDto.threadCapacity` and `UpdateRunnerDto.threadCapacity`. Existing fleet.config.spec expectations unchanged.

**Scope** — In: schema, migration, config flag, runner threadCapacity plumbing, test helper updates. Out: any thread route or service (US-003+), placement use of threadCapacity (US-006), writing tokens/pendingQuestion (B2).

**Interface**
```prisma
model ChatThread {
  id              String    @id @default(cuid())
  projectId       String
  repoId          String
  baseRef         String
  feature         String    // nax feature; branch feat/<feature>
  title           String
  createdById     String
  runnerId        String?   // pinned at the first THREAD assignment, never changed
  backend         Json      // ThreadBackend; immutable
  status          String    @default("ACTIVE") // ACTIVE | ARCHIVED
  archivedAt      DateTime?
  skills          Json      // ThreadSkillSource[] snapshot taken at creation
  maxCostUsd      Decimal   @default(5) @db.Decimal(12, 4)
  costUsd         Decimal   @default(0) @db.Decimal(12, 4)
  tokens          Json?     // { input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite }; written by B2
  specPath        String    // .nax/features/<feature>/spec.md
  pendingQuestion Json?     // { requestId, text, expiresAt }; written by B2
  nextSeq         Int       @default(1)
  lastActivityAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  createdAt       DateTime  @default(now())
  // relations: project (cascade), repo FleetRepo (cascade), createdBy User, runner Runner? (SetNull), messages, turns, jobs
  @@index([projectId, lastActivityAt])
  @@index([runnerId, status])
}

model ChatMessage {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  threadId        String
  seq             Int
  jobId           String?
  turnId          String?
  role            String   // user | assistant
  authorUserId    String?
  clientMessageId String?
  content         String   @db.Text
  toolSummary     Json?
  status          String   // pending | streaming | complete | cancelled | errored | timed_out | interrupted
  errorReason     String?  // set with status errored, at most 200 chars
  usage           Json?
  costUsd         Decimal? @db.Decimal(12, 4)
  costSource      String?
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())
  @@unique([threadId, seq])
  @@unique([threadId, clientMessageId])
}

/// One THREAD job's input (1:1, like FleetConfigEdit for config jobs).
model FleetThreadTurn {
  jobId            String  @id   // FK FleetJob, cascade
  threadId         String        // FK ChatThread, cascade
  action           String        // SESSION | PUBLISH
  initialMessageId String?
  instructions     String  @db.Text
  backend          Json
  skills           Json
  resume           Boolean
}
```
- `FleetJob` gains `threadId String?` (FK `ChatThread`, `onDelete: SetNull`, indexed). `Runner` gains `threadCapacity Int @default(2)`.
- Raw SQL in the migration: partial unique index `ChatThread_active_repo_feature_key` on `("repoId", "feature")` `WHERE "status" = 'ACTIVE'`.

`testFleetConfig` returns a complete `IFleetConfig` literal; it gains `threadsEnabled: false`, because the interface grew a required field and the helper is type-checked by `bun run type-check` (only spec files are excluded).

`PARTIAL_UNIQUE_INDEXES` gains `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "ChatThread_active_repo_feature_key" ON "ChatThread" ("repoId", "feature") WHERE "status" = 'ACTIVE'`, because integration schemas come from `prisma db push`, which cannot create partial indexes; the same statement appears verbatim in the migration (pinned by the partial-indexes unit spec under apps/api/test/unit/fleet).

userStories.title: Thread create, list, get and messages routes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the thread repository, module wiring, create/list/get/messages routes, create-input validation, the skill snapshot, DTOs and i18n.

**Motivation** — Members must be able to open and read a thread against a fleet repo before any session exists; create performs no job work.

**Approach** — All routes live under `projects/:slug/threads` with `ProjectMembershipGuard`, users only (an agent principal gets 403 `threads.principal`, one `assertUser` check per handler).

| Route | Who |
|---|---|
| `POST /` create | DEVELOPER+, checked in the handler after `assertUser` (no `@ProjectPermission` on this route, so an agent key reaches `threads.principal`) |
| `GET /` list (`?status=ACTIVE\|ARCHIVED`, page/size; order `lastActivityAt` desc, `id` desc) | member |
| `GET /:id` | member |
| `GET /:id/messages?afterSeq=<integer >= 0, default 0>&limit=<1..200, default 100>` (ascending `seq`, `{ items }`; out-of-range query -> 400 `threads.input`) | member |

A thread of another project, or an unknown id -> 404 `threads.notFound`. `ThreadDto`: `id, repoId, baseRef, feature, title, createdById, runnerId, backend, status, archivedAt, skills, maxCostUsd, costUsd, tokens, specPath, pendingQuestion, lastActivityAt, createdAt, activeJob: { id, state } | null` (the thread's newest non-terminal THREAD job). `ChatMessageDto`: every `ChatMessage` column except `threadId`.

**Create input** (`thread-input.ts`, errors -> `ValidationAppException({ reason }, 'threads.input')`, HTTP 400): `repoId` (a fleet repo of this project, else 404 `fleet.repos`); `feature` matching `FEATURE_RE` with `feat/<feature>` matching `GIT_REF_RE`; `baseRef` optional, `GIT_REF_RE`, default the repo's default branch; `title` 1..200 characters without control characters; `maxCostUsd` optional, 0.0001..10000 with at most 4 decimals, default 5; `backend` exactly one of `{ kind: 'native', model?, effort? }` or `{ kind: 'acp', agent: 'claude' | 'codex', model?, effort? }` with `model` matching `MODEL_ID_RE`, `effort` matching `/^[a-z]{1,16}$/`, no other keys. Create order: `assertUser` (agent -> 403 `threads.principal`); DEVELOPER+ through the CASL ability for `withProjectRole(principal, ctx.role)` and `can(CREATE, 'FleetJob')` (else 403 `projects`, the guard's usual answer); kill switch (`fleetConfig.threadsEnabled` read on every request, never cached; false -> 409 `threads.disabled`); input; repo; then insert. A duplicate ACTIVE `(repoId, feature)` -> 409 `threads.featureTaken` (`{ feature }`). Create stores `specPath = .nax/features/<feature>/spec.md` and `skills = await skills.snapshotForProject(projectId)`, and creates no job. `ThreadsModule` imports `SkillsModule` (which exports `SkillsService`) and `FleetModule` gains `ThreadsModule` in `imports`.

**Skill snapshot** (`SkillsService.snapshotForProject(projectId): Promise<ThreadSkillSource[]>`, backed by a new `SkillCatalogRepository.listEnabledSnapshot(projectId)` in `skill-catalog.domain.ts` and `prisma-skill-catalog.repository.ts`; `listProjectSkills` stays unchanged): the project's enabled skills grouped by source, sources with a null `resolvedSha` left out, sources ordered by `owner`, then `repo`, then `sourceId`, skills by `name`: `[{ sourceId, owner, repo, sha: resolvedSha, skills: [{ name, dir, description }] }]`.

`ThreadStoreModule` follows the fleet store-module precedent (`ApprovalStoreModule`, `BudgetStoreModule` and `ScheduleStoreModule` export their repository tokens so a sibling module can share storage without a cycle): it exports `CHAT_THREAD_REPOSITORY` to `ThreadsModule` (and later `ThreadJobEffects` to the jobs and sync modules). This is the recorded exception to the `api-data.md` 'repositories are module-private' rule; no module outside `fleet/threads` and those two importers uses the token.

i18n: `apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/threads.json` carries every `threads.*` key from the start: `principal` (403), `notFound` (404), `input` (`-2`, with `{reason}`), `disabled`, `featureTaken` (`{feature}`), `archived`, `costCap`, `runnerOffline`, `runnerOutdated`, `closing`, `turnRunning`, `noSession`, `noQuestion` (409), `notCreator` (403).

The endpoint lifecycle suite `apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` must cover every endpoint (rule api-testing): add POST /api/projects/:slug/threads (201, and 400 for an invalid feature), GET /api/projects/:slug/threads (200), GET /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id (200, 404) and GET /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/messages (200), with FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED=true in that suite's environment; existing expectations unchanged. Regenerate `openapi.json` via `bun run api:export-spec`. Use `seedFleetBase`, `insertRunner`, `seedFleetHttpWorld` from `apps/api/test/helpers/fleet-fixtures.ts`. Reuse `ConflictAppException(args, prefix)`, `ValidationAppException`, `ForbiddenAppException`, `NotFoundAppException`.

**Scope** — In: store module, repository, ThreadsModule, service (create, list, get, messages), controller (those four routes), input validation, DTOs, skill snapshot, i18n, e2e entries. Out: send route and session service (US-004/US-005), stop/end-session/answer/PATCH/archive (US-007), any job creation.

**Interface**
```ts
SkillsService.snapshotForProject(projectId: string): Promise<ThreadSkillSource[]>
SkillCatalogRepository.listEnabledSnapshot(projectId: string): Promise<ThreadSkillSource[]>
// ThreadStoreModule exports CHAT_THREAD_REPOSITORY
```

Integration suites enable the kill switch by setting `app.get(FLEET_CFG).threadsEnabled = true` on the booted app; the services read it on every request.

POST /api/projects/:slug/threads with the repoId of another project's fleet repo answers 404
GET /api/projects/:slug/threads by a project VIEWER answers 200 with the project's threads ordered by lastActivityAt descending
With FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED unset, GET /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id by a project member answers 200
GET /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id for a thread of another project answers 404 with the threads.notFound message

userStories.title: Send message: session start and live input
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `POST /:id/messages` that inserts a user message and either starts a session as a finite `THREAD` fleet job or feeds a live session with a `THREAD_INPUT` command, plus `buildThreadInstructions`.

**Motivation** — Without a job kind to host a session and a command to deliver a message to a running session, there is no way to chat with an agent on a runner.

**Approach** — `POST /:id/messages` `{ text, clientMessageId }`: `text` 1..`THREAD_LIMITS.messageMaxBytes` UTF-8 bytes; `clientMessageId` matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/`. Only the creator sends (403 `threads.notCreator` otherwise). A message of this thread with the same `clientMessageId` already existing -> 200 with `{ message, jobId: null }`, nothing queued (the handler sets the status with `@Res({ passthrough: true })`, since the route's default is 201).

**Lock order (every thread write: send, stop, end session, answer, cap, archive, and `ThreadJobEffects`): job, then thread.** A thread write reads the thread's current job id without a lock, locks that job (`lockById`), then locks the `ChatThread` row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), then re-reads the current job; if it changed, it releases and retries once, and answers 409 `threads.turnRunning` if it changed again. `JobTransitionsService.apply` already holds the job lock when it calls `ThreadJobEffects.onJobEnded`, which then locks the thread, so the two orders agree and a job end cannot interleave with a send that saw the job RUNNING.

Definitions: the thread's **current job** is its newest `THREAD` job in a non-terminal state. A **live session** is a current job in RUNNING with no `THREAD_CLOSE` command at its current `leaseEpoch` (acked or not).

The user message is inserted (`role user`, `status pending`, `authorUserId`, `clientMessageId`, `seq` from `UPDATE "ChatThread" SET "nextSeq" = "nextSeq" + 1 ... RETURNING`), `lastActivityAt = now`, and:

- **live session:** a `FleetCommand` `THREAD_INPUT` `{ messageId, text }` to the current job's `runnerId` at its `leaseEpoch`; after commit `RunnerNotifier.notify(runnerId)`. Response `{ message, jobId: null }`, 201.
- **otherwise:** a `FleetJob` with `command THREAD`, `threadId`, `feature = 'thread-<threadId>'` (so the active `(repoId, feature)` index never meets the thread's own PLAN/RUN on `<feature>`), `ref = baseRef`, `profiles []`, `bashMode raw`, `approvalTimeoutSec` default, `selectorLabels []`, `pinnedRunnerId = runnerId` (null before the first assignment), `maxCostUsd = maxCostUsd - costUsd`, `requestedById = creator`; a `FleetThreadTurn` with `action SESSION`, `initialMessageId`, `instructions = buildThreadInstructions(...)`, `backend` and `skills` copied from the thread, `resume` = the thread already has any earlier `THREAD` job; the QUEUED state event and the `job.dispatched` activity as in `ConfigJobsService.create` (job plus 1:1 input row in one transaction, `apps/api/src/fleet/repo-config/config-jobs.service.ts:117-149`). After commit `placement.placeJob(jobId)`. Response `{ message, jobId }`, 201. A `DuplicateActiveJobError` (a concurrent send won) -> 409 `threads.turnRunning`.

Two concurrent sends are serialized by the `ChatThread` row lock and the active `(repoId, feature)` index on `thread-<id>`. `NewFleetJob`/`FleetJobRecord.threadId` is written by `createJob` in `prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts`. Test fixtures: `insertRunner` in `apps/api/test/helpers/fleet-fixtures.ts` gains optional `protocolVersion` and `threadCapacity` overrides (defaults unchanged: protocol 1, threadCapacity from the column default) and the file gains an exported `THREAD_CAPS` (`FLEET_CAPS` plus `threadBackends: { native: ['m1'], acp: [] }`); existing callers unchanged. Add to `endpoint.e2e.spec.ts`: POST /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/messages (201, and 403 for a non-creator). Regenerate `openapi.json` via `bun run api:export-spec`.

**Instructions** (`thread-instructions.ts`): `buildThreadInstructions({ repo, baseRef, feature, specPath, skills })` (`repo` = `owner/name`) returns these lines joined with `\n`, placeholders filled:
```text
You are a brainstorming partner for the repository {repo} (base ref {baseRef}), working on the feature "{feature}".
Goal: agree with the person on the feature's intent, then draft its spec, which belongs at {specPath}.
How to work:
1. Brainstorm with the person. Ask one question at a time. Read and search the code with your tools before you claim anything about it.
2. When the person agrees the intent is settled, call load_skill with "spec-writing" if it is listed below and follow it. You cannot write files in this session. Put the spec draft in your reply.
3. Then call load_skill with "spec-review" if it is listed below and review the draft against the code.
Tools: list_files and search_repo find files and text; read files with your read tool. You have no shell, no web access and no write access.
Skills available (call load_skill with the name):
- {name} — {description}
```
One `- {name} — {description}` line per snapshot skill, in snapshot order. With no skills the last line is `Skills available: none.` instead of the heading and skill lines.

**Scope** — In: send route happy path (dedupe, message insert, job+turn creation or THREAD_INPUT command), SendMessageDto/SendMessageResultDto, thread-session.service, instructions builder, repository seq/message/job-input/command writes, job domain `threadId`, fixture overrides, e2e entries. Out: the full ordered guard set and `sendRefusal` (US-005) beyond the creator check and dedupe; THREAD placement/assignment and ASSIGN payload (US-006); stop/end/answer/archive (US-007).

**Interface**
```ts
buildThreadInstructions(input: { repo: string; baseRef: string; feature: string; specPath: string; skills: ThreadSkillSource[] }): string
// POST /:id/messages -> { message: ChatMessageDto, jobId: string | null }
```

Integration suites enable the kill switch by setting `app.get(FLEET_CFG).threadsEnabled = true` on the booted app; the services read it on every request.

The same buildThreadInstructions call returns text that includes '.nax/features/add-auth/spec.md'
The same buildThreadInstructions call returns text that includes the sentence 'Put the spec draft in your reply.'
buildThreadInstructions with skills: [] returns text whose last line is 'Skills available: none.'

The first POST /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/messages by the creator with { text: 'hello', clientMessageId: 'c1' } answers 201 with a message whose role is user, status pending, seq 1 and authorUserId the creator
That call creates exactly one FleetJob with command THREAD, threadId the thread's id, feature thread-<threadId>, ref the thread's baseRef, profiles empty, bashMode raw and pinnedRunnerId null
On a thread with maxCostUsd 5 and costUsd 1.25, the first send creates a THREAD job whose maxCostUsd is '3.75'
The first send creates a FleetThreadTurn for the new job with action SESSION, initialMessageId the new message's id, resume false, and backend and skills deep-equal to the thread's

With jest.spyOn(app.get(PlacementService), 'placeJob'), the first send calls placeJob once with the new job's id
On a thread with runnerId R (online, protocolVersion 4) and one COMPLETED THREAD job, a send creates a new THREAD job with pinnedRunnerId R whose FleetThreadTurn.resume is true

On a thread whose THREAD job is RUNNING on an online runner R with protocolVersion 4 at lease epoch E with no THREAD_CLOSE command and no pending message, a send creates no FleetJob and creates one FleetCommand of type THREAD_INPUT for runner R and epoch E whose payload deep-equals { messageId: <new message id>, text: 'hello' }
With jest.spyOn(app.get(RunnerNotifier), 'notify'), a send to a live session on an online runner R with protocolVersion 4 calls notify with R
Repeating a send with the same clientMessageId answers 200 with the same message id, and the counts of FleetJob and FleetCommand rows are unchanged

routing.reasoning: Transactional multi-table writes under a job-then-thread lock order, two send branches, new service and builder; cross-module (jobs, placement, notifier).

userStories.title: THREAD placement
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Place THREAD jobs as their own load class: THREAD misfit rules, server-counted thread slots at sync, ASSIGN payload with `thread`, thread pinning at assign, and THREAD-aware dashboard dry-run.

**Motivation** — Today the fleet knows only finite nax jobs and one job per repo per runner (`busy_repo`); thread sessions are long-lived and must not consume or be blocked by that capacity.

**Approach** — B1-R1: thread slots are counted by the server. The v4 sync request carries no `freeThreadSlots`; on every sync of a runner whose `protocolVersion >= 4` the server assigns QUEUED `THREAD` jobs up to `Runner.threadCapacity` minus the runner's live `THREAD` jobs. B1-R2: today's runner keeps reporting v3, so it never receives a `THREAD` job (placement misfit `protocol`).

Mutations:
- `ActiveJobRef` (`fleet-job.domain.ts:184`): `{ runnerId, repoId, command?: string }`; `PrismaFleetJobRepository.findActiveLoads` always sets `command`
- `RunnerLoad` (`placement-rules.ts:45`): `{ active, repoIds, threads?: number }`; `toLoads` puts a ref whose `command` is `THREAD` into `threads` only, so `active` and `repoIds` count non-THREAD jobs; absent `threads` reads as 0
- `PlacementRunner` (`placement-rules.ts:32`): gains optional `protocolVersion?: number` and `threadCapacity?: number` (absent reads as 0); `findPlacementRunners` always sets both. Optional so the dashboard dry-run (`attention-unplaceable.ts`) and existing spec literals compile unchanged
- `PlacementJob` (`placement-rules.ts:22`): gains `thread?: { backend: ThreadBackend; enabled: boolean }` (set for THREAD jobs)
- `MisfitReason` (`placement-rules.ts:8`): adds `thread_capacity`, `thread_backend`, `threads_disabled` (`protocol` is reused)
- `IFleetJobRepository` (`fleet-job.domain.ts:191`): gains `findThreadAssign(jobId): Promise<ThreadAssign | null>` and `pinThreadRunner(threadId, runnerId): Promise<void>` (sets `ChatThread.runnerId` only when null)
- `buildAssignPayload` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/assign-payload.ts:26`): optional 5th `thread?: ThreadAssign`, copied to `payload.thread`
- `PlacementRunnerRow` (`fleet-job.domain.ts:189`): unchanged shape; carries the new optional `PlacementRunner` fields, which `findPlacementRunners` fills
- `PlacementService.fillRunner` (`placement.service.ts:101`): skips THREAD jobs
- `PlacementService`: gains `fillRunnerThreads(runnerId, now?)`
- `SyncService.sync` (`sync.service.ts:50`): also calls `fillRunnerThreads` when `protocolVersion >= 4`

`toLoads` puts a held `THREAD` job into `threads` only. For a job with `isThreadKind(command)`, `firstMisfit` runs, in order: `disabled`, `offline`, `budget_paused` (as today), `labels` (as today), `executor`, then `threads_disabled` (`job.thread.enabled` false), `protocol` (`runner.protocolVersion < 4`), `thread_backend`, and `thread_capacity` (`load.threads >= runner.threadCapacity`); it skips the profile, sandbox, interaction, approvals relay and tools checks and is exempt from `busy_repo` and `capacity`. `thread_backend`: for `native`, the runner's `capabilities.threadBackends.native` is empty or absent, or a set `model` is not in it; for `acp`, the `agent` is not in `capabilities.threadBackends.acp`. Non-THREAD jobs ignore THREAD jobs for `busy_repo` and `capacity` (through `toLoads`). A THREAD job without `job.thread` (a caller that did not build it) is treated as `threads_disabled`, never a thrown error. The three new misfits are not in `PERMANENT_MISFITS`; `protocol` stays permanent, which does not matter because THREAD jobs are never dispatched through `FleetJobsService.dispatch` and its `evaluatePinned` check. `MISFIT_REASONS` (`apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/dashboard.types.ts:109`) and the `PlacementMisfitDto.reason` enum (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts:107`) gain `thread_capacity`, `thread_backend` and `threads_disabled`. The dashboard dry-run (`jobUnplaceableItems`, `apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/attention-unplaceable.ts`) skips `isThreadKind` jobs; full dashboard treatment of THREAD jobs is B2.

`PlacementService` builds `PlacementJob.thread` from `findThreadAssign(jobId).backend` and `fleetConfig.threadsEnabled`. `assign` passes the `ThreadAssign` to `buildAssignPayload` and, after a successful `casAssign` of a THREAD job, calls `pinThreadRunner(threadId, runnerId)` in the same transaction. `fillRunner` skips THREAD jobs. `fillRunnerThreads(runnerId, now)` locks the runner, computes `slots = threadCapacity - load.threads`, and assigns QUEUED THREAD jobs from the same oldest-first scan window (`QUEUED_SCAN_LIMIT`) while `slots > 0`, honouring pins and the budget pre-assign check like `fillRunner`. `SyncService.sync` calls it after `fillRunner` whenever the sync's `protocolVersion >= 4`, regardless of `freeSlots`.

Regenerate `openapi.json` via `bun run api:export-spec` for the three new `PlacementMisfitDto.reason` values and the dashboard misfit enums. The new optional fields keep the literals in `placement-rules.spec.ts`, `attention-unplaceable.spec.ts` and `attention-rules.spec.ts` compiling with unchanged verdicts; `fleet-job-repository.integration.spec.ts` matches runners with `expect.objectContaining`. `DashboardService` still calls `toLoads` on held refs without `command` (B2 owns that).

**Scope** — In: placement rules, load class, repository methods (`findActiveLoads`, `findPlacementRunners`, `findThreadAssign`, `pinThreadRunner`), PlacementService changes, sync call, assign payload, dashboard dry-run skip and misfit enums. Out: ack/job-end effects and `archivedThreadIds` (US-007); dashboard attention rules for THREAD jobs and runner-load counting in the dashboard (B2); the runner side and package protocol-version bump (B3).

**Interface**
```ts
PlacementService.fillRunnerThreads(runnerId: string, now?: Date): Promise<void>
IFleetJobRepository.findThreadAssign(jobId: string): Promise<ThreadAssign | null>
IFleetJobRepository.pinThreadRunner(threadId: string, runnerId: string): Promise<void>
buildAssignPayload(/* existing 4 params */, thread?: ThreadAssign)
```

Integration suites enable the kill switch by setting `app.get(FLEET_CFG).threadsEnabled = true` on the booted app; the services read it on every request.

userStories.title: Session commands, archive and job-end effects
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add stop, end-session, answer, cap PATCH and archive routes, `ThreadJobEffects` (ack handling and terminal job-end hook), `archivedThreadIds` in the sync response, and the outcome-notification skip for THREAD jobs.

**Motivation** — A person must be able to stop, close and answer a live session and archive a thread, and the thread must reflect command acks and job ends (sweeper, readopt, cancel, runner report) in its messages.

**Approach** — Routes (all under `projects/:slug/threads`, creator-only unless noted, `assertUser` first, 404 `threads.notFound` for other projects):
- `POST /:id/stop` -> `THREAD_STOP_TURN` `{}`; `POST /:id/end-session` -> `THREAD_CLOSE` `{}`; both need a live session (else 409 `threads.noSession`), go to the current job's runner and epoch, and wake the runner (`RunnerNotifier.notify`). Non-creator -> 403 `threads.notCreator`.
- `POST /:id/answer` `{ requestId (1..128), text (1..messageMaxBytes) }` needs a live session and `pendingQuestion.requestId === requestId` (else 409 `threads.noQuestion`) -> `THREAD_ANSWER` `{ requestId, text }`.
- `PATCH /:id` `{ maxCostUsd }` (same bounds as create) sets the thread's cap; it does not change a live session job's `maxCostUsd`.
- `POST /:id/archive`: creator or project ADMIN (`ctx.role === 'ADMIN'`, which includes a global ADMIN); other member -> 403 `threads.notCreator`. Under the job-then-thread lock, `status ARCHIVED`, `archivedAt = now`, committed first; after commit the current job, if any, goes through `FleetJobsService.cancel(actorId, projectId, jobId, true)` (QUEUED or never-acked ASSIGNED end CANCELLED on the server; otherwise `cancelRequestedAt` and one `CANCEL`). A send that takes the locks after the archive sees ARCHIVED (check 4). A 409 `fleet.jobState` from `cancel` (the job ended between the commit and the cancel) is ignored. Archiving an archived thread returns 200 unchanged. Archive is also the way to free a first session left QUEUED because no runner fits (stop needs a live session).
- Stop, end session and answer re-check the live session under the job-then-thread lock (see lock order below), so two concurrent end-session calls queue one `THREAD_CLOSE`.
- Lock order (every thread write): job, then thread. Read the current job id without a lock, `lockById` the job, then `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` the `ChatThread`, then re-read the current job; if changed, release and retry once, and 409 `threads.turnRunning` if it changed again. A **live session** is a current job in RUNNING with no `THREAD_CLOSE` at its current `leaseEpoch` (acked or not).
- Sync response `archivedThreadIds`: ids of ARCHIVED threads whose `runnerId` is the syncing runner, newest `archivedAt` first, at most `THREAD_LIMITS.maxArchivedThreadIds`, read through `ThreadJobEffects.archivedThreadIds(runnerId)`. The runner prunes their directories (B3).
- `ThreadStoreModule` now also exports `ThreadJobEffects` to the jobs and sync modules; `FleetJobsModule` (`fleet-jobs.module.ts`) and `SyncModule` (`sync.module.ts`) add `ThreadStoreModule` to `imports`.
- `ThreadJobEffects` (`thread-job-effects.ts`) writes through the module-private thread repository (`CHAT_THREAD_REPOSITORY`), which gains `replaceCommandPayload(commandId, payload)` for the `FleetCommand` rewrite. `JobTransitionsService` and `CommandAckProcessor` take it as their **last** constructor parameter, so existing specs that construct them positionally keep working once they pass a stub; their calls are guarded by `isThreadKind` / the command type.
  - `onInputAck(command, result, detail)`: for `THREAD_INPUT`, the command payload becomes `{ messageId }`; on `rejected` the message's `status` becomes `errored` with `errorReason = detail` (at most 200 chars). For `THREAD_ANSWER`, the payload becomes `{ requestId }`. `CommandAckProcessor.processOne` (`command-ack.processor.ts:48`) calls it for those two types after the fence check, inside the ack transaction, and returns no live job event.
  - `onJobEnded(job)`: called by `JobTransitionsService.apply` (`job-transitions.service.ts:42`) for every terminal transition (COMPLETED, FAILED, ESCALATED, CRASHED, CANCELLED) of a job with `isThreadKind(command)` and a `threadId`, in the same transaction: the thread's messages in `pending` or `streaming` become `errored` (`content` kept, `errorReason` = the job's state lowercased, e.g. `crashed`) and `pendingQuestion` becomes null. After a clean idle close no message is in flight, so nothing changes.
  - `errorReason` can carry runner-supplied text; the web (B4) renders it as plain text.
- B1-R4: `FleetJobOutcomeRecorder.onTerminal` (`job-outcome.recorder.ts:21`) returns without enqueueing for a `THREAD` job (no `fleet_job_outcome` row).
- `SyncService.sync` response gains `archivedThreadIds`.

Add to `endpoint.e2e.spec.ts`: POST /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/stop (409 without a live session), POST .../end-session (409), POST .../answer (409), PATCH /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id (200) and POST .../archive (200). Regenerate `openapi.json` via `bun run api:export-spec`. SEAM-5: the terminal hook is triggered via the scheduled `FleetSweeper.sweep(now)` against a silent runner; acks are posted through `POST /api/fleet/runner/sync`.

**Scope** — In: the five routes and DTOs, `ThreadJobEffects`, repository `replaceCommandPayload`/archived reads, module imports, ack branch, terminal hook, outcome-recorder skip, `archivedThreadIds`, e2e entries. Out: setting `pendingQuestion`, message completion, cost accrual (B2); Publish and `THREAD_PUBLISH` creation (phase C); runner-side handling (B3).

**Interface**
```ts
class ThreadJobEffects {
  onInputAck(command, result, detail): Promise<void>; // types follow the ack processor's existing ones
  onJobEnded(job): Promise<void>; // the existing FleetJobRecord
  archivedThreadIds(runnerId: string): Promise<string[]>;
}
// ThreadRepository: replaceCommandPayload(commandId: string, payload: unknown): Promise<void>
// UpdateThreadDto { maxCostUsd }, AnswerQuestionDto { requestId, text }
```

Integration suites enable the kill switch by setting `app.get(FLEET_CFG).threadsEnabled = true` on the booted app; the services read it on every request.

analysis:
Feature B1 of fleet S5a phase B: API-only core of brainstorm threads. All stories are workdir apps/api, except US-001 also touches packages/fleet-protocol (type-only consumers in the API; apps/api production code must use `import type` from the package, pinned by protocol.spec.ts, so runtime values are mirrored in apps/api/src/fleet/common/thread-jobs.ts as config-jobs.ts mirrors packages/fleet-protocol/src/config-jobs.ts; specs import the package at runtime to pin parity).

KEY EXISTING CODE (verified on main 2969dcf4): FleetJobsService.cancel (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts:140); BudgetGate.assertNotPaused (budgets/budget-gate.ts:16) + jobGateKeys (budgets/budget-rules.ts); isRunnerOnline (fleet/common/runner-online.ts); RunnerNotifier.notify (jobs/runner-notifier.ts); FEATURE_RE/GIT_REF_RE (jobs/dispatch-input.ts:9-11); controller pattern in fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.controller.ts (ProjectMembershipGuard, @ProjectPermission, @CurrentProject, isUserPrincipal, casl.createForUser(withProjectRole(...))); config-job pattern (job + 1:1 input row in one tx, then placement.placeJob) in fleet/repo-config/config-jobs.service.ts:117-149; store-module precedent in fleet/schedules/schedule-store.module.ts (ApprovalStoreModule, BudgetStoreModule, ScheduleStoreModule); placement in jobs/placement-rules.ts (PlacementJob:22, PlacementRunner:32, RunnerLoad:45, MisfitReason:8, firstMisfit:92) and jobs/placement.service.ts (fillRunner:101); sync in sync/sync.service.ts:50; acks in sync/command-ack.processor.ts:48; terminal hooks in jobs/job-transitions.service.ts:42; outcome recorder jobs/job-outcome.recorder.ts:21; sweeper sync/fleet-sweeper.ts:48; dashboard misfits dashboard/dashboard.types.ts:109 and dashboard/attention-unplaceable.ts.

BINDING RULINGS: D541 members read all threads, only the creator acts (send, stop, end session, answer, raise cap), archive is creator or project ADMIN (ctx.role==='ADMIN', includes global ADMIN); agent API keys refused 403 threads.principal on every thread route via one assertUser per handler. B1-R1 thread slots are counted by the server (v4 sync carries no freeThreadSlots; assign QUEUED THREAD jobs up to Runner.threadCapacity minus live THREAD jobs; threadCapacity server-only via admin PATCH). B1-R2 package FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 3; API accepts 4. B1-R3 paused budget -> existing 409 fleet.budgetPaused. B1-R4 THREAD jobs never enqueue fleet_job_outcome. B1-R5 FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED default false, read from fleetConfig.threadsEnabled on EVERY request (never cached at construction) so integration suites toggle app.get(FLEET_CFG).threadsEnabled.

LOCK ORDER (every thread write: send, stop, end session, answer, cap, archive, ThreadJobEffects): job, then thread. Read the thread's current job id without a lock, lockById the job, then SELECT ... FOR UPDATE the ChatThread row, then re-read the current job; if changed release and retry once, then 409 threads.turnRunning. JobTransitionsService.apply already holds the job lock when calling ThreadJobEffects.onJobEnded, which then locks the thread, so orders agree.

SEND CHECK ORDER is implemented once as pure sendRefusal(state) in thread-send-rules.ts (US-005) and the service throws the matching exception. US-004 builds the send happy path (message insert with seq from UPDATE ... nextSeq+1 RETURNING, THREAD job + FleetThreadTurn in one tx, or THREAD_INPUT FleetCommand for a live session); US-005 adds the ordered guards and requeue refusal.

PLACEMENT: THREAD is its own load class (RunnerLoad.threads); toLoads puts held THREAD refs (ActiveJobRef.command) into threads only, so non-THREAD busy_repo/capacity ignore them. New optional fields (RunnerLoad.threads, PlacementRunner.protocolVersion/threadCapacity, ActiveJobRef.command, PlacementJob.thread) keep existing spec literals compiling. fillRunner skips THREAD jobs; fillRunnerThreads(runnerId, now) locks the runner and assigns QUEUED THREAD jobs within QUEUED_SCAN_LIMIT; SyncService.sync calls it for protocolVersion >= 4 regardless of freeSlots. assign passes ThreadAssign to buildAssignPayload and pinThreadRunner in the same tx after a successful casAssign.

TEST INFRA: integration suites build schema from schema.prisma via prisma db push (cannot create partial indexes) so PARTIAL_UNIQUE_INDEXES in apps/api/test/helpers/partial-indexes.ts must gain the ChatThread partial unique index verbatim as in the migration (pinned by a unit spec under apps/api/test/unit/fleet). testFleetConfig (apps/api/src/common/test-helpers/fleet-config.ts) must gain threadsEnabled:false or type-check fails. protocol.spec.ts literals (kinds, commands Record<Union,true>) must be extended or compile fails. insertRunner/THREAD_CAPS fixtures in apps/api/test/helpers/fleet-fixtures.ts (US-004). The endpoint lifecycle e2e (apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts) must cover every new endpoint (rule api-testing) with FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED=true. After each contract-changing story run `bun run generate` / api:export-spec to refresh committed openapi.json; never edit apps/cli/src/generated. i18n: apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/threads.json carry every threads.* key from US-003. nax run notes: DB-backed tests need compose test Postgres (`bun run test:db:up` in apps/api).

RISKS: (1) deadlock if lock order job-then-thread is violated anywhere; (2) FleetJob.threadId added to NewFleetJob/FleetJobRecord affects every FleetJobRecord literal in specs; (3) JobTransitionsService and CommandAckProcessor take ThreadJobEffects as LAST constructor param so positional specs keep working with a stub; (4) widened unions in packages/fleet-protocol must still compile for apps/runner (build gate for US-001: `bun run type-check` at repo root); (5) THREAD jobs must never go through FleetJobsService.dispatch/evaluatePinned; requeue refuses them; (6) errorReason can carry runner-supplied text (max 200 chars, plain text); (7) migration must default existing Runner rows to threadCapacity 2.
outOfScope: The `thread` log stream, durable ingest (`ThreadIngestCursor`), a user message becoming `complete`, assistant messages, cost and token accrual, setting `pendingQuestion`, and the content-carrying SSE belong to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-ingest` (B2).
`THREAD` in budget hard stops (`BUDGET_STOP_COMMANDS`), thread spend in fleet analytics (`NAX_JOBS`), and dashboard attention rules for `THREAD` jobs belong to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-ingest` (B2).

The runner session host, worktree, tools, skill fetch, the runner's `threadBackends` report and READOPT handling of `THREAD` jobs belong to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-runner` (B3), which also bumps the package `FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` to 4; this feature leaves it at 3.
Thread pages, composables and navigation belong to feature `fleet-s5a-thread-web` (B4).
`write_doc`, Publish (`THREAD_PUBLISH` is declared but never queued; no `action: PUBLISH` job is created), Plan and Run from a thread, and `threads.busy` belong to phase C.
ACP backends are accepted at create and matched by placement, but no runner reports them before phase D.
A resume job pinned to a runner that stopped reporting the thread's backend waits QUEUED; no misfit is surfaced on the thread.
Moving a thread to another runner, thread delete, search and export, editing a past message, turn notifications and CLI commands.
Deleting a runner sets the threads' `runnerId` to null (`SetNull`); the next session is placed afresh with `resume: true`, and the runner side treats a missing transcript as a fresh session (B3).
QUEUED THREAD jobs share the oldest-first `QUEUED_SCAN_LIMIT` window with other jobs; a large backlog of one kind can delay the other within a fill.
